invariants.requirement: Every authorization decision is computed from current server-side grants at request time; a role or permission change takes effect immediately, without re-issuing or re-reading the access token.
A missing role or permission is refused with the same generic AUTH_FORBIDDEN response in the canonical error envelope, without revealing which grant was required.
Authentication is resolved before authorization: an absent, invalid or unusable session yields 401, never 403.
Authorization is deny-by-default: a route declaring a requirement is refused unless the principal holds it, while a route declaring none stays available to any authenticated principal.
Every authorization denial emits a business audit event through the baseline audit port, without recording the missing grant in the public response.
The authorization summary exposes only the effective role and permission codes of the current principal, sorted and free of internal identifiers.
The client consumes the authorization summary for conditional rendering only; it never treats it as an authorization proof, the authority remaining the API on every request.
The summary is requested only for an authenticated session and is never stored in a shared or reusable cache across sessions.
No token and no internal server structure leaks through the authorization surface, including on error.
